title: Brown Rice with Carrots and Dark Green Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain product that retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than white rice. In this dish it is combined with carrots and dark green vegetables (such as broccoli, spinach or kale), boosting the content of vitamins, minerals and dietary fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice provides more fiber, B‑vitamins and magnesium than white rice.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark green vegetables are among the best sources of vitamin K, folate and antioxidants.
The combination of whole grains and vegetables gives a longer feeling of fullness.
When stored properly, brown rice can stay fresh for up to 6 months.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the whole grain and vegetables promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Rich source of vitamins
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots and vitamin K and folate from green vegetables help maintain vision, blood clotting and cell growth.

items.title: May lower cardiovascular risk
items.content: Magnesium and potassium from the rice and vegetables support normal blood pressure and heart function.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Antioxidants (carotenoids, polyphenols) protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: Brown rice has a lower GI than white rice, helping to keep blood sugar levels steadier.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Whole grains contain phytic acid, which can reduce the absorption of certain minerals if consumed in very large amounts.

items.title: Vegetable allergies
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to carrots or specific green vegetables.

items.title: Food safety with improper storage
items.content: If rice is stored in a humid environment it can mold; cooked rice left at room temperature for more than 2 hours may become a breeding ground for bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish as a side to meat, fish or tofu, or enjoy it as a light main course. Cook the rice until tender, then stir‑fry it with sliced carrots and dark green vegetables. Optionally season with soy sauce, ginger or a squeeze of lemon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry brown rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 6 months. Refrigerate cooked portions and consume within 3 days, reheating until steaming hot.
